manual_verification_result.net: PASS -- the attendee badge renders and behaves as built. Note that 'as built' is a lower bar on this arm than on its three siblings; see the two structural notes below, both of which are known and were ruled on at their gates, not defects found today.

checks.MV-5 badge renders on a 15-minute card: PASS -- and this is the point: this arm has NO size gate, so it renders where all three sibling arms deliberately suppress

manual_verification_result.structural_note_1_no_size_gates: Unlike all three sibling CMP-105 arms, this implementation has no MIN_HEIGHT or MIN_WIDTH threshold whatsoever -- the cards render the badge on any event with a non-empty attendees array. This is NOT an acceptance-criteria violation for this run: its ACs (requirements.md section 'Acceptance criteria', items 1-8) are entirely test-existence and suite-green criteria and never asked for a size gate, where the sibling arms' requirements did. The practical consequences cut both ways and are worth keeping for the comparison. Upside: the feature is visible out of the box on the stock 30-minute demo standup, where the opus-plus-flash-v37 arm's identical-looking feature renders NOWHERE on a freshly seeded database because its 52px gate suppresses it. Downside: nothing stops the badge appearing on a 15-minute sliver where it competes with the title for a card that has room for neither.
manual_verification_result.structural_note_2_raw_email_fallback: AttendeeBadge.tsx uses `a.displayName ?? a.email`, so an attendee with no display name has their RAW EMAIL ADDRESS written into both the per-dot hover title and the group aria-label -- on the grid, which is on screen at rest and lands in every screenshare and screenshot. This is security finding F-1. It was NOT missed: the reviewer raised it, asked for an explicit Gate ruling, and Gate 3 ACCEPTED IT AS DEBT for this comparison arm while listing it must-fix-before-merge. All three sibling arms refused this by construction -- opus-plus-sonnet degrades an unnamed attendee to the literal 'Guest', opus-plus-flash-v37 whitelists a single letter-or-digit monogram so no attendee-supplied string reaches the DOM at all, and opus-only-v5's label function takes (status, count) and is structurally incapable of emitting an identity. This arm is the only one of the four that puts an email on the always-visible surface.
manual_verification_result.f1_confirmation_status: The functional checks above were confirmed by hand. The F-1 raw-email fallback was NOT independently confirmed by observation in this pass -- it stands on the code at AttendeeBadge.tsx (the `?? a.email` expression in both the title and the summaryLabel) and on the Gate 3 ruling that accepted it. A future pass wanting to observe it directly should seed an attendee with displayName null and read the card's accessible label.
manual_verification_result.pre_existing_bug_not_a_finding_against_t: Test data was written directly into IndexedDB, bypassing the app's save path, because in local / anonymous mode any move, resize or edit destroys the attendee list outright (baseline bug MV-01, recorded on run 20260822-062945, still unticketed). Not caused by this run; it constrains how the feature can be hand-tested.
manual_verification_result.not_closed_by_this_check: None of the run's must-fix-before-merge follow-ups are closed by this check, F-1 and F-2 included. Nothing was verified with a screen reader.

rollback.reason: provenance.json holds 7 entries for 6 unique paths: AttendeeBadge.tsx appears twice (created by tp_cg_003_r2, then edited by tp_refine_r1). The second entry records existed_before:true with a backup_path. A reverter keying on the LAST entry per path would RESTORE that backup instead of DELETING the file, leaving a pre-refinement AttendeeBadge.tsx on disk. This is the known antigravity-worker provenance hazard, reproduced concretely.
rollback.verified: All 6 sha_after values were checked against the real files on disk: 0 mismatches. The record is accurate; it is the multi-entry replay semantics that are unsafe.
